name: lotor
description: A local receipt and approval gate for AI agent sessions. The agent can act, but it cannot sign.
long_description: A local-first, MCP-native receipt layer for AI agent sessions. It writes a signed, tamper-evident log of what an agent did during a session (actions performed, files touched, messages sent, costs incurred, failures encountered) and exposes tools to query those receipts, verify chain integrity, and run a fail-closed gated action that requires an owner-signed approval token.

lotor_home.title: Receipt store location
lotor_home.description: Where Lotor writes your receipt chain and keys. Keep it on local disk. A synced cloud folder hands your receipt log to a third party, which is the custody Lotor exists to remove. Defaults to a .lotor folder in your home directory.

tools.name: query_receipts
tools.description: Query receipt summaries from the chain (most recent first). Optional params: limit, sessionId.

tools.name: sessions_since
tools.description: What happened while you were not looking. Summarises every session in the chain since a point in time, grouped by session, with what each ran and which files it touched. Call it before asserting something has not been built: concurrent sessions cannot see each other and the chain is the only place their work is visible. Idle sessions are counted, not listed. Gate decisions carry no session id and are reported unattributed. Params: since, excludeSessionId, includeQuiet, limit.

tools.name: verify_chain
tools.description: Verify chain integrity. Returns { ok, brokenAt?, reason?, entryCount }.

tools.name: lotor_status
tools.description: Report runtime status: store location, receipt count, chain integrity, herding mode, whether the signing gate is set up, and whether the recording and gating hooks are actually registered. A key without a registered hook means nothing is gated.

tools.name: gated_action
tools.description: Fail-closed gate. Denies an action unless a valid owner-signed approval token is presented for that exact action, and writes a receipt to the chain in both directions (denied and approved). Params: action, optional params, optional approvalToken.
